applications.name: Chronic non-healing diabetic foot ulcer: autologous platelet-rich plasma gel (adjacent wound-care application)

classifications.name: Wagner / University of Texas grade
classifications.summary: Depth-based grading of diabetic foot ulcers from superficial (grade 1) to bone involvement and gangrene; PRP gel trials enroll non-infected, non-ischemic ulcers.

applications.why_biologic: Platelet-derived growth factors in a gel applied to the wound bed to speed granulation and closure; the only musculoskeletal-adjacent PRP use with a national Medicare coverage determination.
applications.autograft_standard: No graft. Standard of care is debridement, offloading, infection and perfusion management; becaplermin (rhPDGF-BB gel) is the approved biologic comparator.
applications.volume_note: No reliable US count of PRP-treated wounds; Medicare coverage started 2021-04-13 for chronic non-healing diabetic wounds (CMS NCD 270.3).

products.name: Arthrex ACP Double Syringe System and ACP Max PRP System
products.ownership_history: Privately held (Naples, FL). Arthrex sells its own ACP line and, separately, distributes the Angel cPRP/marrow system (see arthrex-angel). The Genesis Biologics AAPS 510(k) cites the Arthrex Double Syringe (ACP) System (BK190406) as its predicate, so ACP is the reference device for newer ORG clearances.
products.composition: Single-use double-syringe device: venous blood is drawn into the outer syringe, spun in a benchtop centrifuge, and the plasma fraction is drawn into the inner syringe (generally described as a leukocyte-poor, low-platelet PRP). An independent benchtop test of four kits (GPS III, SmartPReP2, Magellan, ACP) found three buffy-coat kits at 3-6x baseline platelets and one plasma-sampling kit at only 1.5x; the abstract does not name that kit, but ACP is the plasma-sampling design. ACP Max (2022) is the successor system.

regulatory.reference: BK070069 (Arthrex Double Syringe (ACP, Autologous Conditioned Plasma) System, decision 2008-12-12, FDA product code FMF 'Syringe, piston', 21 CFR 880.5860); BK190406 (Arthrex Double Syringe (ACP) System, 2019-11-06); BK210655 (Arthrex ACP Max PRP System, decision 2022-09-22, product code ORG, 21 CFR 864.9245). CBER-reviewed BK numbers, not K numbers.
on_label_indications: BK210655 sits in product code ORG, whose FDA definition is 'preparation of autologous platelet rich plasma from a small sample of peripheral blood for mixing with bone graft to improve handling characteristics'. Arthrex's own ACP Max summary text was not retrievable; the wording is the ORG classification definition.
The first ACP clearance (BK070069) was filed as a piston syringe (880.5860), not as a platelet separator: the 2008 clearance carries no therapeutic indication at all.

Not cleared for injection into knees, tendons or any soft tissue. Regulatory frame for every PRP kit: 510(k)s in product code ORG (21 CFR 864.9245) clear the device to prepare PRP 'to be mixed with bone graft' at the point of care to improve handling; older JQC, KSS and FMF clearances cover a centrifuge, a blood-bank supply or a piston syringe and carry no therapeutic indication. Injection of PRP into a joint or tendon is an off-label use of the device. FDA has not approved or cleared PRP as a treatment for those uses; the autologous preparation sits outside premarket review (361-exempt, same-surgical-procedure rule) only while it stays minimally manipulated.

products.challenge: A hiring manager will ask why a device cleared as a piston syringe and a bone-graft-handling kit is sold for knee and tendon injections, and and how a plasma-sampling, low-platelet preparation compares with buffy-coat PRP.

applications.evidence_summary: Best brand-specific evidence is negative: a double-blind single-center RCT (n=120 knees, 30 per arm, PRP prepared with the Arthrex ACP-System) found no evidence that PRP, hyaluronic acid or glucocorticoid beat placebo for pain over 6 months (Tschopp 2023).
applications.caveats: Single center, low baseline pain (median NRS 32.5), early-stage OA; the ACP-System is a plasma-based, low-platelet preparation. Class-level: meta-analyses of PRP vs HA (Belk 2021, 18 RCTs) favor PRP while the largest placebo-controlled RCT (Bennell 2021, n=288) was negative. Off-label injection use.

applications.evidence_summary: No published study of this product in this application located (PubMed and ClinicalTrials.gov search 2026-10-23). Class-level, product-unspecified RCTs in lateral epicondylitis are mixed (Mishra 2014 n=230 positive at 24 weeks only; Peerbooms 2010 n=100 positive vs corticosteroid).
applications.caveats: Several investigator-initiated ACP trials are registered (Tampere NCT01851044 lateral epicondylitis n=120; Bispebjerg NCT02417987 Achilles n=60; McMaster NCT01668953 terminated) but no published report naming the Arthrex device was confirmed. Off-label.

applications.evidence_summary: No published study of this product in this application located (PubMed and ClinicalTrials.gov search 2026-10-23). Registry shows a Schulthess Klinik ACP rotator cuff repair RCT (NCT01266226, n=129, completed) but no report confirmed by search.
applications.caveats: Class-level: PRFM and PRP augmentation of cuff repair has been neutral in RCTs (Rodeo 2012 n=79, Castricini 2011 n=88). Off-label.

applications.evidence_summary: No published study of this product in this application located (PubMed and ClinicalTrials.gov search 2026-10-23).

evidence.title: A Randomized Trial of Intra-articular Injection Therapy for Knee Osteoarthritis
evidence.finding: Double-blind single-center trial of glucocorticoid, HA, PRP (prepared with the Arthrex ACP-System) or placebo, 30 knees per arm, KL 1-3: no evidence that any active injection beat placebo for pain within 6 months.

evidence.title: Analysis of Platelet-Rich Plasma Extraction: Variations in Platelet and Blood Components Between 4 Common Commercial Kits
evidence.finding: Class-level, includes ACP: Benchtop test of GPS III, SmartPReP2, Magellan and ACP (Device Technologies) on blood from 3 donors: three kits sampling the buffy coat gave 3-6x baseline platelets and white cells while one plasma-sampling kit gave only 1.5x (the abstract does not say which kit; ACP is the double-syringe design that draws plasma).

evidence.title: Platelet-Rich Plasma Versus Hyaluronic Acid for Knee Osteoarthritis: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis of Randomized Controlled Trials
evidence.finding: Class-level (product not named): 18 level-1 studies (811 PRP, 797 HA patients): WOMAC total improvement 44.7% vs 12.6%; leukocyte-poor PRP gave better IKDC than leukocyte-rich.

evidence.title: Efficacy of platelet-rich plasma for chronic tennis elbow: a double-blind, prospective, multicenter, randomized controlled trial of 230 patients
evidence.finding: Class-level (product not named): Leukocyte-enriched PRP needling vs active control: no difference at 12 weeks (pain improvement 55.1% vs 47.4%, p=.163); at 24 weeks 71.5% vs 56.1% (p=.019) and success 83.9% vs 68.3% (p=.037).

evidence.title: Positive effect of an autologous platelet concentrate in lateral epicondylitis in a double-blind randomized controlled trial: platelet-rich plasma versus corticosteroid injection with a 1-year follow-up
evidence.finding: Class-level (product not named): PRP vs corticosteroid: VAS success 73% vs 49% at one year (p<.001); the platelet-concentrate system is not named in the abstract.

evidence.title: Application of rhBMP-7 and platelet-rich plasma in the treatment of long bone non-unions: a prospective randomised clinical study on 120 patients
evidence.finding: Class-level (product not named): Persistent long-bone nonunions: union in 86.7% with rhBMP-7 vs 68.3% with PRP; PRP was the weaker arm.

products.composition: Threaded bone marrow aspiration needle sold alongside the Angel system for iliac crest and other marrow harvest; a harvest accessory, not a concentrator.

products.composition: Celution is an automated closed system that digests lipoaspirate with Celase enzyme to isolate adipose-derived regenerative cells (a stromal vascular fraction product). Puregraft (50, 250, 850) is a washing/filtering fat-graft device without enzymes.

regulatory.reference: Celution Cell Concentration Device K060482 (2006-09-28, product code CAC, autotransfusion/cell washing) and Cytori Lipoplasty System with Celase K063235 (2007-01-24, QPB, fat emulsification; Celase reagent) cover tissue/cell handling, not therapy. Puregraft 250/850/50: K092923, K113255, K132815 (MUU) for aesthetic fat grafting. Orthopedic ADRC use only in IDE trials such as NCT02326961.
on_label_indications: K060482: collection, concentration, washing and reinfusion of autologous cells collected intra- or postoperatively (general, orthopedic and other surgery); K063235: fragmentation, emulsification and aspiration of soft tissue and aesthetic body contouring. Neither authorizes ADRC injection for osteoarthritis. Enzymatic ADRC/SVF is a 351 drug under FDA's 2017 and 2020 guidance, so injection outside an IND is off-label/unapproved (US v. US Stem Cell Clinic, 11th Cir. 2021).
